newsitem.title: BRAZIL: ROWING-OXFORD/CAMBRIDGE MAY STAGE AMAZON BOAT RACE.
newsitem.headline: ROWING-OXFORD/CAMBRIDGE MAY STAGE AMAZON BOAT RACE.

text.p: Oxford and Cambridge Universities' rowing crews look set to stage a boat race on Brazil's Amazon river on September 21 this year, Britain's ambassador to Brazil, Keith Haskell, said on Tuesday.

"We have talked to the Amazonas state government which is organising the sponsorship and to the Brazilian Rowing Federation and both universities have confirmed their crews are available," Haskell said.
The race is being organised as part of a series of cultural and sporting events in the run-up to Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's state visit to Britain in December.
One of the main problems has been organising two eights boats for the race, Haskell said.

Those available in Rio de Janeiro and Sao Paulo cannot be split into sections. At one point organisers considered using military aircraft to fly the boats but the boats are one metre too long, he added.
Now it looks as if two new boats which can be split into sections will be bought. After the race, they would be left in the Amazon capital of Manaus to help develop the sport.
There could also be a second race with Brazilian rowers against a mixed Oxford/Cambridge crew, Haskell said.
One other possible Anglo-Brazilian event being discussed is a football match between former English and Brazilian stars, including Pele, at Wembley stadium.
"Pele has never played at Wembley. I have been talking to him and he is quite interested provided I can get Bobby Charlton to play," Haskell said.
"One possibility would be to have the match in August as a curtain-raiser to the Football Association Charity Shield match," he added.
